rationale: Reviewed 7404845f401f4839d4ddec0ce3969d65ac9270fe, the complete panel BRIEF, my Round-4 verdict, consolidated-round-4.md, the revised R1/R4/R6 contracts and ACs, ADR-0045 and relevant existing git/panel/readiness/reattest code. The audited identity tuple and mandatory read-time revalidation close the two original stale-audit mechanisms. However, the replacement F2 rule treats independent panel-local round counters as a chronology and lets an abandoned common-ancestor registration raise the acceptance threshold. Two real-git probes using the shipped panel.Create, Scan and ForBead reproduce those contract counterexamples without audit forgery. A third contract counterexample shows malformed matching-tuple audits cannot be repaired by the specified convergent no-op. Five existing reattest safeguards and one MF-1 mapping probe passed; seven R6 contract checks passed. Structural spec validation exited 0 with only the no-beads-epic warning. The proposed fallback implementation does not exist yet: the F2/no-op results are explicit models of the written specification, not claims of shipped implementation exploits. All writes and git mutation probes were confined to my assigned scratch directory; the source worktree was not modified.
concrete_changes_required: Revise R4.2 F2, its ADR-0041 amendment contract and AC-11 so round values from independent registration directories are not assumed to establish review chronology. The current panel writer starts every new slug at round 1 and imposes no bead-global ordering. Fail closed for an outside-tip registration whose supersession by an accepted anchor cannot be established; an earlier-rebased-review exception must use a demonstrated ordering relationship, rather than the numeric maximum across arbitrary slugs. Add a real-git AC with landed A registered in original-panel at round 4, then genuinely later unlanded B registered in new-review at the normal default round 1, with the bead branch absent or reset to A. Both fresh fallback reattest and read-back of an otherwise valid matching audit must refuse without writing. Preserve primary-path behavior and the existing scoped-override/attested-restore exits. This need not introduce authentication or a new panel substrate: conservative refusal is sufficient when the existing records cannot prove ordering.

Constrain F2's positive anchor authority: an abandoned registration must not raise the highest anchor round and thereby suppress a visible unlanded review. Generic ancestry alone also does not demonstrate the specific post-review completion relationship used to justify the ancestor exception. Define which completion-related ancestor evidence can supersede another review, and fail closed when that relationship is not established. Add AC-11 fixtures with an exact landed A at round 1 and outside-tip B at round 2, then an abandoned round-3 registration at common ancestor C whose tree omits A's work. Adding C must not change refusal into acceptance, either in reattest or automatic read-back. Retain a positive fixture for the actual #233 completion-descendant shape, rather than removing ancestor support indiscriminately. Apply these constraints in the lifecycle consumer; do not globally remove abandoned panels from panel.ForBead or change its existing gate contract.

Qualify R4.2's fallback convergent no-op by audit validity as well as tuple equality. When binding == candidate == stored audit tuple but op/at/actor is missing or malformed, fresh reattest must rerun F1-F5 and replace the malformed audit with a valid record, even though the pair is unchanged. Add a malformed-matching-tuple recovery leg: initial MF-3 refuses; explicit reattest writes a valid audit; MF-3 passes; a subsequent fully valid same-tuple reattest is Wrote=false. Preserve the unchanged primary-path no-op test. Update AC-11 and AC-18's amendment pin accordingly.

findings.title: Round-4 ask status
findings.detail: G3r4.1 PARTIAL: spec.md:402-412 and :427-430 now require F1-F5 on every read-back; AC-11(xiv)-(xvi) pin a post-audit revert, later review and added candidate. Thus the original bypass of current checks is closed. However, the requested outside-tip-review refusal has been replaced by the narrower F2 round rule, and the independent-slug and abandoned-anchor counterexamples below still admit genuinely unlanded review evidence. This is a defect in the replacement predicate, not a claim that read-back still skips F2. G3r4.2 ADDRESSED: :420-430 binds separately recorded accepted merge/second-parent identity to both current binding and scan-derived candidate, validates audit shape, and forces a write when the tuple is absent/different. AC-11(xii), (xiii), (xi) and (i-r) pin stale executor replacement, malformed refusal, same-pair missing-audit recovery and valid no-op respectively. The malformed-matching-tuple repair issue below is new.

findings.title: F2 mistakes independent panel rounds for a review chronology
findings.detail: spec.md:404-408 compares every outside-tip registration's round with the highest anchor round across panel.ForBead's set. cmd/mindspec/panel.go:329 defaults each new slug to round 1; internal/panel/create.go:134-143 simply records the caller's round in that directory; neither writer nor scanner supplies bead-global sequence or cross-directory supersession. Atomic co-bumping of round and reviewed SHA within one panel does not establish ordering between different panels. TestG3R5IndependentSlugRoundIsNotChronology creates real landed M/A, moves M off first-parent through a real main carrier, makes later unlanded B descending from A, and deletes bead/probe-one. It then uses the shipped panel.Create to register original-panel {A, round 4} followed by new-review {B, round 1}. Real git confirms B is outside the spec tip, M remains reachable off first-parent, the single landing's content is present, and no surviving bead ref contradicts it. The literal F2 predicate accepts because 1 < 4. Fresh reattest can therefore vouch for the old landing despite genuinely later visible unlanded work, and mandatory revalidation cannot rescue subsequent automatic reads because it repeats the same predicate. No metadata audit forgery, false git ancestry or hand-edited round is needed. Probe: repo/internal/lifecycle/g3_round5_probe_test.go:79; output: probe-results.txt.

findings.title: An abandoned ancestor registration can turn F2 refusal into acceptance
findings.detail: spec.md:405 calls any registration at any ancestor of the second parent an anchor, without an abandonment or completion-equivalence condition. panel.ForBead at internal/panel/panel.go:269-279 intentionally includes abandoned registrations. TestG3R5AbandonedAncestorRaisesAnchor first registers exact landed A at round 1 and unlanded B at round 2; the written F2 correctly refuses. Adding a well-formed abandoned round-3 registration at common ancestor C then changes F2 to acceptance: C is an ancestor of A, so maxAnchor becomes 3 and B's round 2 is dismissed. The real C and A trees differ, and C contains none of A's introduced work; this is not the #233 tree-identical completion step used to justify the ancestry expansion. The abandoned flag and its reason are present and survive the real Scan/ForBead lookup. An irrelevant abandoned review has gained positive authority to suppress an otherwise blocking review. The same git fixture passes F1/F3/F4 and needs no fabricated audit; reattest can issue a genuine one after the flawed check. Probe: repo/internal/lifecycle/g3_round5_probe_test.go:91; output: probe-results.txt. This finding concerns positive supersession authority in the new F2 consumer, not authentication of panel.json or changing the existing panel gate's treatment of abandoned panels.

findings.title: Matching-tuple no-op leaves malformed audit unrecoverable through reattest
findings.detail: spec.md:425 makes reattest a convergent no-op when the stored tuple equals the binding and candidate. It does not require the rest of the audit to be VALID. But :428 rejects an audit with a wrong op, invalid timestamp or empty actor even when its tuple matches. With a real safe candidate, correct binding and matching audit tuple but op='wrong', explicit reattest runs its checks and selects the specified no-op, leaving the same unusable audit. MF-3 still fails and its first recovery is reattest again. AC-11(xiii) only asserts malformed read refusal; (xi) only repairs an absent tuple, and (i-r) only covers a valid no-op. The small written-contract check in override-contract-probe.py demonstrates the incompatible predicates. This is an unimplemented contract repair gap, not a claim that the current pre-129 reader implements the tuple. A fully valid matching audit should retain no-op behavior; invalid audit fields should be regenerated on explicit successful fallback reattest.

findings.title: Audited tuple, accepted residual and override scope
findings.detail: The tuple now prevents an authentic M1 audit from inheriting authority over an executor replacement binding M2. Read-back requires exact agreement with the independent scan and repeats current ambiguity, surviving-tip, revert and read checks. A metadata-only forge is explicitly allowed to reach only what reattest would accept, and its bounded new reach is honestly stated at spec.md:434-437. I request no signing, external authority or hard block for that acknowledged residual. The remaining high findings are faulty acceptance predicates reachable with genuine registrations and a genuine subsequent audit. R6 still stores failing-intersect-named signals, replaces rather than unions markers, uses per-record subset coverage, excludes indeterminate failures and denies marker-based claim authority. Seven contract checks passed for explicit scope, added dependency, shrinkage, indeterminate failure, named-but-passing signal, blocker source and multiplicity; no new override widening was found within the specified failure-record identities. These are checks of the written schema-v2 contract, not tests of an implemented schema-v2 reader.

findings.title: PlanMapsBead adversarial check
findings.detail: The AND-plus-positional definition matches current MF-1's actual structural prerequisites. TestG3R5PlanMappingMatchesMF1Structure calls shipped extractBeadSectionRaw and evaluateMF1: the second heading labelled Bead 12 maps positionally to N=2; a concrete matching chunk passes; a missing chunk or a chunk without a section fails. The revised shared-helper contract therefore closes the previous half-mapped-membership gap. Content checks remain readiness failures, and lineage/dispatch consistency is still required before any deliberate N4 MF-1 override. No new cross-spec claim authority was found. Probe: repo/internal/validate/readiness/g3_round5_probe_test.go; output: mapping-results.txt.

findings.title: Verification and limits
findings.detail: Scratch clone is detached at 7404845f401f4839d4ddec0ce3969d65ac9270fe. Two new real-git F2 contract probes and five existing lifecycle safeguards passed: TestReattest_HappyPathFleetState, TestReattest_ContradictoryBindingOverwrittenAudited, TestReattest_RevertedRefuses, TestReattest_MaskedRevertOldestAnchored and TestReattest_StaleOlderRemergeBindingRewrittenToNewest. The MF-1 structure probe passed. override-contract-probe.py passed seven R6 checks and reproduced the malformed-audit no-op contract mismatch. go run ./cmd/mindspec validate spec 129-readiness-tracker-honesty exited 0 and printed only '[WARN] lifecycle-binding: spec has no beads epic; run spec approve to create one' (validate-results.txt). No full implementation suite or future fallback-reader execution is claimed. All probe sources, caches, logs and temporary git repositories were created under the exact assigned scratch path. The source repository's reviewed HEAD remains unchanged.
